transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Cleveland, Ohio, I'm Dale Willman.
President Trump will be campaigning in Iowa and Kansas Sunday.
Both states have critical Senate races that could help decide which party controls the body next session.
Speaking during a rally in Florida, Friday night, Trump talked about how grueling campaigning can be.
You know, I'm going to Kansas. I'm going to Kansas. We're going to be. You watch.
We're going to have a little meeting in Iowa. They said, could I go? Great candidates.
I thought this was going to be my last one, Byron. I thought this was it.
I thought I could relax. 28 days in a row, this crap is a lot. It's a lot.
With days left until the midterm elections, anti-Islam rhetoric in the Michigan Senate race has increased.
NPR's Jason Derose reports on the Muslim community's response.
Democrat Abdul Al-Sayed, whose Muslim is facing Republican candidate Mike Rogers.
In recent days, President Trump has accused Al-Sayed without evidence of being a jihadist
and a member of the Islamist group, the Muslim Brotherhood.
Executive director of Michigan's Council on American Islamic Relations Dawood Walid calls the accusations horrific.
In my 21 years of being with the Council on American Islamic Relations, I have never seen this level of racism and anti-Muslim animus in our political discourse.
Walid says the Islamophobic rhetoric makes everyday Muslims feel dehumanized and afraid.
Jason Derose, NPR News.
Parts of the American Southwest are still recovering from flooding after thunderstorms dropped massive amounts of rain last week.
From member station KNAU, Chris Clements reports that rural communities and tribal nations are bracing for another round of stormy weather.
Arizona election officials say they're concerned about the ability of Navajo Nation residents to reach polling places after previous floods wiped out roads.
Arizona Governor Katie Hobbs says she's considering all options to help counties dealing with the disaster, which prompted evacuations and caused tornadoes to touch down.
We've been in constant communication with emergency managers at the county level and at the tribal level, providing support where we can.
This weekend's storm could cause more flooding on the Navajo and Hopi reservations, starting Saturday night into early Monday morning.
For NPR News, I'm Chris Clements in Flagstaff.
Evacuations began Friday from the war-ravaged Ukrainian city of Oleshki.
The estimated 2,000 residents that are remaining in the city were offered the choice of traveling to either Ukrainian or Russian-controlled territory.
Evacuations, rather, began on the fourth day of a local truce, but Ukraine's president says Russian attacks continued elsewhere, including a drone attack in northeast Ukraine Friday that killed one person and injured eight others.
Stocks closed down across the board Friday. This is NPR News.
At least one person has died after a shooting in Fairfield, California Friday night.
Six others were transported to area hospitals with gunshot wounds.
Police have released little information about the shooting, which took place at a Spirit Halloween store in a Solano town center.
They say it is still under active investigation.
A small AI satellite launched by Google earlier this month has answered its first query, and NPR's Jeff Brumfield has more on that story.
The AI chip circling above the Earth composed a haiku for humans back home.
Blue marble below it wrote, "Data streams in silent grace. Starlight feeds my core."
Followed by the sparkles emoji because even in space, AI loves an emoji.
The haiku was posted by Google CEO Sundar Pichai on X. Google eventually hopes to build orbital data centers.
The launch of this chip is a small first step, but experts say a huge amount of work and potentially hundreds or even thousands of satellites will be needed.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
Prosecutors in Texas have charged an ICE agent with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
Officials say Officer Mario Alberto Morales was driving an unmarked SUV when it hit 48-year-old Miguel Para Hernandez.
Para Hernandez broke his leg in his infederal custody.
ICE says Para Hernandez ran out in front of the officer's car, but prosecutors say video of the incident contradicts that account.
In college football, DJ Lagway threw for 319 yards as Baylor pounced UCF Friday night, winning 41-9.
And in an Ivy League classic, Dartmouth beat Harvard 24-14.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: President Trump plans to campaign in Iowa and Kansas Sunday ahead of midterm Senate races
Anti-Islam rhetoric rises in Michigan Senate race between Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers
Flooding recovery continues in Arizona as Navajo Nation faces another storm threat
Evacuations begin from war-damaged Ukrainian city of Oleshky under local truce
At least one dead and six wounded in Fairfield, California Halloween store shooting
Google's small AI satellite answers its first query with a haiku
Texas prosecutors charge ICE officer Mario Alberto Morales with aggravated assault in Miguel Para Hernandez case
Baylor beats UCF 41-9 led by DJ Lagway's 319 passing yards
Dartmouth defeats Harvard 24-14 in Ivy League football
